changes.after: Reshaping changes how a table is laid out while keeping the measurements.

before: A wide table stores day1 and day2 in separate columns. A long table stores a day identifier and one minutes column, with repeated id values. This changes the layout, not the underlying measurements.

reshape uses varying for the measurement columns, v.names for their shared value name, timevar and times for the new occasion labels, and idvar for the entity identifier. direction = "long" selects this conversion. Verify unique entity/occasion pairs before trying a reverse wide transformation.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
wide <- data.frame(id = c("a", "b"), day1 = c(10, 20), day2 = c(15, 25))
long <- reshape(wide, varying = c("day1", "day2"), v.names = "minutes",
                timevar = "day", times = c(1, 2), idvar = "id", direction = "long")
cat(nrow(long), "\n")
cat(sum(long$minutes), "\n")
```

Expected output or behavior: 4
70. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Inspect long$id and long$day to identify each observation before reshaping back. You may trace it without a R interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
